title: PlanBench-XL: Long-Horizon Planning in Large Tool Ecosystems
hook: A benchmark of 1,665 tools shows top agents plan fine until tools start failing silently — then GPT-5.4's success crashes from 52% to 11%.
key_points: 327 interactive retail tasks over 1,665 tools; agents must retrieve relevant tools, not see them all upfront.
Tasks need iterative tool use — each call surfaces evidence the next call depends on, over long horizons.
A 'blocking' mode injects missing, failing, or distracting tools to simulate real-world unpredictability.
GPT-5.4 reaches 51.9% accuracy without blocking but collapses to 11.36% under the most severe blocking.
Agents fail most when failures give no explicit error signal or recovery needs a longer alternative path.
content_html: LLM agents increasingly operate inside large tool ecosystems, where a task means discovering the right tools, chaining their outputs, and adapting when things go wrong. PlanBench-XL, from Liu, Ji, Hakkani-Tür and colleagues, is an interactive benchmark of 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools designed to test exactly that — and crucially, it doesn't hand the agent every tool upfront.
extra_html:
What it tests

Agents must iteratively retrieve usable tools and invoke them to uncover the evidence later steps depend on, over long horizons. An optional "blocking" mechanism injects missing, failing, or distracting tool functions to mimic real-world unpredictability, forcing the agent to notice a broken path and adapt at runtime. This is the gap the authors target: prior benchmarks rarely evaluate planning under retrieval-limited tool visibility.

What they found

Across ten leading models, massive-tool planning stayed hard. GPT-5.4 managed 51.90% accuracy in the block-free setting but collapsed to 11.36% under the most severe blocking. The analysis points to two failure modes: agents are especially vulnerable when failures carry no explicit error signal, and when recovery demands a longer alternative path. PlanBench-XL is offered as a testbed for diagnosing these adaptive-planning failures.

related.hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

related.title: Why One Engineer Dropped Embeddings for BM25 in Tool Selection
related.hook: An engineer running an agent with ~140 tools dropped embedding-based tool selection for plain BM25 — cosine similarity over short tool descriptions was dangerous in production.

related.title: Agents' Last Exam: Benchmarking Agents on Real Economic Work
related.hook: Frontier agents ace academic benchmarks but flop on real jobs — Agents' Last Exam scores them on 1,000+ economically valuable workflows, where the hardest tier sees just a 2.6% pass rate.

flashcards.prompt: Why does PlanBench-XL hide tools behind retrieval instead of listing all 1,665 upfront?
flashcards.back_html: Real agents in large ecosystems must first discover which tools are relevant; retrieval-limited visibility tests planning under partial information, which a fixed tool list doesn't.

flashcards.prompt: What did PlanBench-XL's 'blocking' condition reveal about leading LLM agents?

choices.text: Accuracy collapsed — GPT-5.4 fell from ~52% to ~11% — once tools could fail, go missing, or distract
Agents performed about equally well with and without tool failures
Adding more tools always improved accuracy

flashcards.explanation_html: Block-free, GPT-5.4 scored 51.9%; under the most severe blocking it dropped to 11.36%, showing how brittle long-horizon planning is when the environment is imperfect.

flashcards.prompt: When are these agents most likely to fail at long-horizon tool use?
flashcards.back_html: When a failure comes with no explicit error signal, or when recovery requires finding a longer alternative tool-use path.
